Being an instance of a class distinct from another entity does not contradict being part of that entity.
Sharing a mother or father across child/sibling relations is compatible with both original parent claims.

Service specialization and disputed-region policy paths require several unsupported transfers and do not negate the original ownership/membership claims.

Only one unit directly conflicts; the other units rely on invalid overlap/division/border transitivity, so the four-conflict label is unsupported.
Shape, subclass, contains, and disjoint/incompatible relations are composed across different semantic types without licensed rules.
